name: gla_decay_rescaled_chunk_api
hypothesis: GLA's chunked prefill carries its gate around as an explicit exponential TILE and then computes the same k-v contraction twice. (1) The gate as a tile: the output stage forms the intra-sub-chunk scores as a raw q @ k^T and then multiplies them by a full (G, num_sub, sub, sub) matrix of gate ratios -- it materializes log_diff = s_log[..., :, None] - s_log[..., None, :], exponentiates it, and multiplies, three passes over a tile as large as the score tile itself (8 MiB at gla-long) -- and pays a fourth pass rescaling the inter-chunk term by exp(s_log - entrance). (2) The contraction, twice: chunk_fwd_h_kernel_varlen computes k^T v over its OWN (H, T, K)/(H, T, V) transposes to build the (NT, H, K, V) chunk-entrance buffer, and the output stage then computes k^T v again, per sub-chunk, to build the sub-chunk entrance states -- so k and v are streamed twice, the buffer is written and re-read, and the state stage pays a whole XLA stage for arithmetic that is a rounding error next to it. Measured in-process under the gate's own deterministic-XLA flags at the DP-selected plans (gla-long chunk_size=2048, gla-short 512, both output_value_tiles=8, compact), the state stage is 34.1% of gla-long and 18.5% of gla-short, and the whole call moves about 256 MiB of fp32 intermediates for 2.2 GFLOP -- it is paying for tiles it forms, not for the arithmetic they hold. This capability introduces a STANDALONE JAX API -- decay_rescaled_chunk_fwd in the new file python/sgl_jax/srt/kernels/simple_gla/simple_gla_decay_rescaled.py -- that removes both costs with one identity. The gate g_gamma is a per-head SCALAR decay, so exp(s_i - s_j) factors as exp(s_i - a) * exp(a - s_j) around any pivot a; taking a to be the sub-chunk entrance and rescaling ONLY the column side, k_hat = k * exp(a - s), makes q . k_hat already carry the decay, so the score tile needs its causal MASK and nothing else, and the row half exp(s_i - a) -- which multiplies the intra term and the inter term alike -- rides out to the single output scaling instead of paying its own pass. The same k_hat gives w = k_hat^T v, which is simultaneously the sub-chunk's state contribution AND, summed onto the chunk's real exit, the chunk carry itself: so the second contraction, the state stage, its transposes, its buffer and its round trip all disappear and ONE launch consumes q/k/v and emits both the token output and the final recurrent state. Nothing is approximated -- it is the same sum re-associated. Every exponent formed on the q side and on the state side is a later-minus-earlier difference (non-positive); the only growing factor is exp(a - s_j) on k_hat, whose span is bounded by ONE sub-chunk (|gamma| * 128, about e^12.8 for the repo's gate range) and which always meets its matching row factor inside the same dot product, so retained products are identical to the shipped ratio form and the discarded strictly-upper ones are masked. Following the round-8 finding that a predicated region costs more than the stage it guards, the body is STRAIGHT-LINE: the sequence-entrance reset, the padded tail and the final-state write are selects and masked contraction weights, not pl.when regions. Deployment goes through a free-named string dispatch control gla.chunk_impl whose default 'incumbent' leaves the shipped two-stage pipeline untouched and bit-identical. All 48 new deployable configurations were run: every one matches the frozen pure-JAX fused_recurrent_simple_gla reference to at most 8.3e-6 on both compared outputs (token output and final recurrent state) against a 1e-3 tolerance.

estimate.reasoning: SHARE: from the last completed target-hardware eval (evals/c1786023097_round_011), taking its RETAINED-INCUMBENT branch since that round was rejected and its code reverted. tiny-linear-serving is the only model holding non-deferred cases on this backend (the other two defer all 10 of their calls), so it is 100% of the three-model aggregate; its per-callsite costs at the incumbent plan are kda-long 1.2219ms (51.22%), kda-short 0.4322ms (18.12%), input-projection 0.3456ms (14.49%), gla-long 0.2766ms (11.60%), gla-short 0.1091ms (4.57%), summing to 2.3854ms. Both of this action's callsites are in that model, so the addressable share is 16.17%. LOCALIZATION: measured in-process under the gate's own deterministic-XLA flags (--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0 --xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true), with jax.clear_caches() between variants so the inner jit of chunk_simple_gla_fwd_varlen retraces, deleting the state stage from the pipeline removes 34.1% of gla-long and 18.5% of gla-short while deleting the output stage removes 54.7%/38.9% and the alignment 8.4%/0.5% -- the two stages this handle merges are 88.8% of gla-long and 57.4% of gla-short. The optimized HLO confirms the cost is the tiles, not the flops: gla-long launches 5 fp32 gemms totalling 2.2 GFLOP but moves about 256 MiB of fp32 intermediates, and the sub-chunk height is already at its byte optimum (a sweep of 32/64/128/256 measured 0.2285/0.1695/0.1574/0.1838ms, so 128 is kept). MEASURED, one warmup then twelve alternating-order paired runs of the full runner entry (median of each side, ratio = exp(median(log(candidate/incumbent)))): gla-long at its DP-selected incumbent plan (cs=2048, compact, ovt=8, batched_value_tiles output, decay-matrix state) is 0.2319ms and its best decay_rescaled configuration (cs=2048, compact, ovt=8) is 0.1708ms, paired ratio 0.7173 = 28.27% relief; gla-short at its incumbent plan (cs=512, compact, ovt=8) is 0.0953ms against 0.0797ms, paired ratio 0.8001 = 19.99% relief. AGGREGATE = 0.1160*28.27 + 0.0457*19.99 = 3.28 + 0.91 = 4.19%. DISCOUNT: reported as 3.5%, cutting about a sixth, because the gate re-selects plans on both sides of the pair and because part of the win is the removal of launched XLA stages, which a deterministic TPU schedule rewards less than this GPU-interpret proxy does. The same share-weighted method predicted 8.5% for round 9 against a measured paired 9.31% and 70% for round 8 against 75.64%, so it is calibrated conservative; the >2% bar is cleared even if only gla-long improved and only by half the measured amount. NOT A REPEAT OF A FAILED ESTIMATE: the two recorded simple_gla estimate failures were on enable_chunk_fwd_h_kernel_varlen_variant (one a workload-fingerprint rejection since fixed by the harness's deterministic XLA flags, one a manifest schema slip) and one on state_output_impl; none proposed chunk_impl. The rejected round-11 state_output_impl action also fused the two stages, but it kept the shipped gate-ratio tile and only moved the state recurrence into the output kernel; it measured 21.3% modeled relief on gla-long (0.2766 -> 0.2176) where the decay-rescaled factorization measures 28.27% paired, because removing the ratio tile and the duplicate contraction is a different and larger saving than relocating the stage. NOVELTY: run through the frozen akt.core.analysis.api_metrics score path on both affected cases, the candidate scores mass=90 (compute 51, memory 39) with largest connected delta component 82 and zero_embed=0, against this family's calibrated per-case floor of 0 (effective minimum 4) on gla:seq512_h8 and gla:seq2048_h8 -- PASS on both. SPACE: the handle owns the whole recurrence, so its configurations pin enable__chunk_fwd_o_pl_variant, enable_chunk_fwd_h_kernel_varlen_variant and output_impl at their defaults, and its two-level walk bounds chunk_size to multiples of the 128-row sub-chunk above one sub-chunk; the runner therefore enumerates 32 new configurations for gla-long and 16 for gla-short (320->352 and 224->240, 764->812 campaign-wide) while every incumbent configuration is preserved exactly at the new dimension's default.
